info.bio:
The Damned es un grupo de Punk y más tarde Rock gótico formado en Londres, en 1976.

Fueron la primer banda punk inglesa en lanzar un sencillo (New Rose), sacar un álbum (Damned, Damned, Damned), y recorrer los Estados Unidos. La música de sus comienzos (más o menos entre 1976 y 1980) y en especial el estilo de batería de Rat Scabies fueron una gran influencia para la creación del Hardcore punk en los Estados Unidos. The Damned han sido considerados también como unos de los fundadores del rock gótico.

scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La gira de los Ramones de 1976 contagia a Inglaterra, donde el punk es combinación de moda y paro: la Gran Bretaña de Thatcher, con las ciudades industriales devastadas, convierte el «punk» en algo mucho más serio que lo que pretendían los Ramones. Malcolm McLaren inventa el sonido (Sex Pistols, «los Ramones con heroína y valium») y la imagen. The Clash, los más intelectuales (London Calling, Sandinista); Damned, Generation X, Buzzcocks (inventores del punk-pop), Vibrators. En Australia, Radio Birdman y los Saints. La segunda ola (GBH, UK Subs, Neurotics, New Model Army, Stiff Little Fingers) y el punk anarquista (Crass, Discharge, Rudimentari Peni, Subhumans).

podcast.title: 100 Club Punk Rock Festival Performance (September 20, 1976)
podcast.body: The Damned performed at Britain's first official punk rock festival, held at the 100 Club on Oxford Street, London. Their participation, alongside the Sex Pistols and The Clash, was instrumental in bringing punk rock out of secrecy and into wider public awareness. "This was the site of Britain's first official punk rock festival."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First British Punk Record (1976)
podcast.body: The Damned earned the distinction of becoming the first British punk band to release a record, a significant achievement following their inspiration from the Ramones' London shows in July 1976. "the damn who would become the first British punk band to release a record"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Witnessing The Ramones (July 4, 1976)
podcast.body: The Damned, who would become the first British punk band to release a record, were present at The Ramones' July 4, 1976 gig at the Roundhouse in London. They were among those "transformed by what they saw and heard." "the damn who would become the first British punk band to release a record... They were all at these gigs and they were all transformed by what they saw and heard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Punk Rock Single (N/A)
podcast.body: The British group The Damned holds the distinction of being the first punk rock band to release a single, predating the Sex Pistols' debut. "That honor goes to a British group called The Damned."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Garage Rock Core
podcast.body: The Damned are categorized as having a Garage Rock core due to their "back to basics approach," linking them to the fundamental characteristics of the genre amidst the punk movement. "The sex pistols, the clash, the damned, all those groups are garage rock bands at their core because of their back to basics approach."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 4: Garage Rock

podcast.title: Grizzled Veteran Participant
podcast.body: The Damned, an English punk band from the 1970s, joined the Warped Tour, demonstrating that the festival also attracted established and older acts. "There was the damned, yes, the English punk band from the 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pioneering DIY Approach
podcast.body: The Damned's release of "New Rose" proved that bands could bypass major labels and "make a record ourselves" with a minimal budget, championing a "do it yourself" (DIY) approach that convinced many groups to be more proactive in recording and releasing music. "This DIY, this do it yourself approach, preached by the Damned, convinced many groups to take a much more proactive approach when it came to recording and releasing music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Recording at Wessex Studios
podcast.body: The Damned recorded at Wessex Studios, an old church hall in North London known for its live sound, which was a popular choice among punk and post-punk bands. "A lot of punk bands and post punk bands, like using the place, the clash and the damned and suzy and the banshees and the pretenders and the specials and generation X and the sex pistols."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sid Vicious Audition
podcast.body: Sid Vicious was considered for the lead vocalist position in The Damned but failed to show up for the audition. "Sid was considered for lead vocalist of the damned, but me forgot to show up for the audition."

podcast.title: Sid Vicious Considered for Lead Singer – Missed Audition
podcast.body: Sid Vicious was considered to be the lead singer of The Damned, a new punk band at the time. However, he failed to show up for the audition and did not get the gig. "It's also possible that he was considered to be the lead singer of another new punk band called The Damned."

podcast.title: Vampire Claim
podcast.body: Dave Vanian, the singer of the punk band The Damned, sometimes claimed to be a vampire, which was noted as an interesting detail in the context of the emerging Goth scene. "Some remembered that Dave Vainian of the punk band The Damned, sometimes claimed to be a vampire, which, and I was pretty interesting."

xref.title: Conquest of England (July 4 & 6, 1976)
xref.body: The Ramones played two pivotal shows in London, first at the Roundhouse (capacity 2,000) on America's bicentennial, and then at Dingwalls two nights later. Despite their European record company trying to cancel gigs, the band delivered explosive performances. These concerts were England's "first proper exposure" to US-style punk rock and are credited with transforming nearly every major player in the burgeoning British punk rock scene, including members of the Sex Pistols, The Clash, The Pretenders, The Damned, and Generation X. "And over the course of those two nights, July 4th and July 6th, 1976, just about every single person who would become a major player in the British punk rock explosion were taught a lesson by the Ramones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: One-Off Band for a Single Show – Late August 1978
xref.body: Sid Vicious put this band together and played only one show at the Electric Ballroom in London in late August 1978. The lineup included Rat Scabies of The Damned on drums and Glenn Matlock, the Sex Pistols' former bassist, on bass, with Sid on vocals. "Sid put together a band and played one show at the Electric Ballroom in London in late August of 1978."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Catalyst for British Punk Explosion
xref.body: The Ramones' two London gigs in July 1976 are considered foundational for the British punk rock explosion. Major figures like Johnny Rotten, Sid Vicious, Joe Strummer, Chrissy Hynde, The Damned, and Billy Idol were in attendance and were profoundly "transformed by what they saw and heard," inspiring them to form their own bands. "Over the course of those two nights, July 4th and July 6th 1976, just about every single person who would become a major player in the British punk rock explosion were taught a lesson by the Ramones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Chrissie Hynde's Punk Credentials
xref.body: Lead singer Chrissie Hynde, originally from Akron, Ohio, moved to the UK and became deeply involved in the early punk scene, working at Malcolm McLaren's shop "Sex" and playing guitar in bands that morphed into The Clash and The Damned, even considering a marriage of convenience with Sid Vicious. "So yeah, a lot of bonafide punk credentials."

xref.title: Early Gloomy Incarnation
xref.body: In their initial phase, Ultravox was quite gloomy, contributing to the dark music that attracted early goth adherents before the band lightened up considerably. "Ultravox, who would later lighten up considerably, were quite gloomy in their first incarnation, making songs like Saturday Night in the City of the Dead, and the Wild, the Beautiful, and the Damned."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Canadian Band to Sign to Stiff Records – Power Pop Side of Vancouver Punk
xref.body: The Pointed Sticks formed in Vancouver in 1978, five former members overlapping with D.O.A. and the Subhumans. Their sound was more melodic and power pop-leaning than their contemporaries — five members singing harmonies was unusual in punk. Their name came from a Monty Python sketch about self-defense against pointed sticks. They became the first Canadian band to sign to Stiff Records in the UK, home to the Damned, Nick Lowe, Elvis Costello, and Ian Dury. Several strong singles and one album followed. Their relative accessibility broadened the audience for Vancouver punk. "Stiff Records, one of the groundbreaking indie labels in the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Fundraising Gig for New York Move
xref.body: Formed as a temporary group featuring Sid Vicious on vocals, Glenn Matlock (whom Sid had replaced in the Sex Pistols) on bass, Rats Scabies of The Damned on drums, and Steve New on guitar, this group played a quick solo gig at the Electric Ballroom in Camden on August 15, 1978. The purpose was to raise money for Sid and Nancy to fly to New York. "To raise money, there was a quick solo gig at the electric ballroom in Camden under the name Vicious White Kids."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Glass-Throwing Incident at 100 Club
xref.body: On the second day of the 100 Club Punk Special in September 1976, while The Damned were performing, a speed-intoxicated Sid Vicious threw a glass aimed at Dave Vanian, the singer. He missed Vanian but hit a woman in the face, blinding her in one eye, which led to Sid's first prison sentence. "He missed hitting a woman in the face and blinding her in one eye. That led to Sid's first taste of prison."
